Access Oracle REST resources as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__oracle_ords.R
oauth_db_oracle_ords_api.Rd

Read Oracle data through Oracle REST Data Services (ORDS) using each visitor's access token. ORDS exposes tables and custom database handlers as web APIs. This client calls those APIs over HTTPS without Oracle client libraries.

Usage

oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(
  authorization,
  url,
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  timeout = 30,
  ca_bundle = NULL,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

url

HTTPS ORDS schema base URL, including any proxy prefix, for example "https://data.example.org/ords/reporting".

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

timeout

Maximum seconds for one request, including its refresh retry.

ca_bundle

Optional path to a trusted CA certificate bundle.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A client object with these methods:

  • $select(resource, query = list(), raw = FALSE) reads one page of records from an AutoREST collection. Pass query parameters such as list(limit = 20L, offset = 0L).

  • $request(path, method = "GET", query = list(), body = NULL, raw = FALSE, trailing_slash = FALSE) calls a JSON resource. Supply relative path segments, for example c("api", "sales"). Set trailing_slash = TRUE when the resource URL ends in /.

Details

Configure ORDS to trust your provider's JWT access tokens and map their scopes or roles to resource privileges. Create the client inside server() and call its methods from render or reactive expressions.

ORDS controls access to its endpoints. The token's user ID is available to handlers as :current_user, but it doesn't automatically change the Oracle database schema. Configure handler filtering or a database security context to apply the required per-user data access.

Results are JSON lists, including items, hasMore and pagination links. Large integers stay as strings. Fetch pages explicitly; the client doesn't follow links or redirects. raw = TRUE and HEAD return an httr2 response; successful empty responses otherwise return invisible NULL.

Requests use a current token and discard results after sign-out or account changes. GET and HEAD can refresh and retry once after HTTP 401; writes don't retry automatically.

See also

oauth_db_oracle(), vignette("oracle-ords", package = "shinyOAuthDB").

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ords <- oauth_db_oracle_ords_api(
  auth$connection, "https://data.example.org/ords/reporting"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderPrint({
  ords$select("orders", query = list(limit = 20L))$items
})
} # }
